name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
short: Raises the chance of liver enzyme elevation, especially at high doses or with antiseizure drugs. Raises a clobazam metabolite and may interact with drugs using CYP450 enzymes.
text: In a meta-analysis of clinical trials, cannabidiol was associated with more liver enzyme elevations and drug-induced liver injury than placebo, with high doses (1000 mg/day or more, or 20 mg/kg/day or more) and concomitant antiepileptic drugs as risk factors; no severe cases were reported, and none were reported in adults taking under 300 mg/day. In a healthy-volunteer study, cannabidiol raised exposure to the clobazam metabolite N-desmethylclobazam about 3.4-fold, with no clinically relevant effect on valproate levels. A systematic review found reported interactions between cannabinoids and warfarin, valproate, tacrolimus and sirolimus, and notes that interactions are likely with prescription drugs that use the same CYP450 enzymes.

quotes: Cannabidiol use was associated with an increased probability of liver enzyme elevation
High-dose CBD (≥1000 mg/day or ≥20 mg/kg/day) and concomitant antiepileptic drug use were identified as risk factors.
No cases were reported in adults using cannabidiol doses <300 mg/day. No cases of severe DILI were reported.
